notes: Written against script.md (script a, revised 2026-09-29 without the handedness beat, B4) and take5@1.08.words.json, which narration.json names. Beat ids keep their numbers: B1, B2, B3, B5, B6.
Geometry is px in the 1080×1920 frame, origin top-left; points are [x, y].

Frame 0 is the hook: the whole mirror scene is visibleAtStart (mirror, the person in it, me from behind) under the first caption. The mirror fills the visual zone (x 160–920, y 270–1220), so the picture is as big as the zone and every beat ending on the mirror scene is centered by its frame.

B1's Display drops the spoken '거울은' (script.md, approved 2026-09-29) because the frame-0 picture is the mirror: the first chunk '왜 위아래는 안 뒤집을까요?' is the whole question in 4 eojeol and 644 px, anchored on '거울은' and drawn from frame 0. With '거울은' it was 5 eojeol and 814 px, over the chunk limit and the 800 px line.

Mirror scene camera: behind me and above my left shoulder, looking into the mirror. Perspective is one vanishing point, VP (182, −49), above the frame. The person in the mirror is me scaled by s = 38/85 = 0.447 about the VP (head (580, 1000) → (360, 420); raised hand (741, 838) → (432, 348)), so my hand, the mirror surface on that line ((528, 500), scale 2s/(1+s) = 0.618), and the mirrored hand lie on one straight line through the VP. B3's two front arrows ride that line. Production may retune the layout; keep the person in the mirror on the scaled copy (same VP and s) so the front arrows stay collinear, and move the ghost's B5 spot and the arrows with it.

Drawing rules from research.md (Easy to misstate): the person in the mirror is never drawn as me turned around. Its raised hand is on the same screen side as mine (to the right of its body), it shows a palm where mine shows a back, and each hand's thumb points toward its own body's midline, so both thumbs are on the screen left of their hands: the same outline. It is never labeled 오른손. B5's turned-around ghost is the figure that differs (raised hand on the screen left). The lake (B6) is scenery only: a mountain and a tree, no person.

Hand faces are colored from frame 0 (B1's 'both raised hands in accent colors'): the back of a hand blue, a palm yellow with palm lines. B3 pulses them instead of repainting, so no color changes its meaning mid-episode.

Arrow colors follow one rule: teal is a direction along the mirror's surface (unchanged in the mirror: up and right while it stands), purple is the direction into the mirror (the one it flips). Laid flat as a lake, the direction into the surface is vertical, so the lake's vertical arrows are purple and its horizontal ones teal.

Hidden, not exited: me, reflection, frontMe and frontRefl leave the screen (or dim) with setStyle {opacity} and come back with opacity 1 (the purple pair from B5 to B6's '거울로'; me dimmed through B5; the people from B6's lake to the loop), because an exited id can't come back. Everything else exits. The mirror scene itself stays from B1 through B5.

Loop: the last frame is the first. Both show the mirror standing (tilt 0) with its sheen at rest, the person in the mirror and me at full opacity, and nothing else: no arrows, rings, ghost, big hands, label or scenery. frontMe and frontRefl are still alive at the end but at opacity 0.

Draw order is declaration order: mirror < me < reflection (I stand in front of the glass and cover its bottom edge; me and the person in the mirror never overlap), then everything declared later on top, except the ghost, drawn beneath the person in the mirror (props.beneath): over me as it turns, behind the mirror person's legs as it walks in. The person in the mirror is drawn only on the glass (props.inside), so it never shows outside the mirror while the mirror stands back up in the loop.

An element is invisible until its appear cue, unless it has visibleAtStart. Cues sharing an anchor run in parallel, except that an appear waits for the exits on its anchor to finish. Every exit is a 0.2 s even fade. setStyle is not an entrance: a restore on the same word as an exit cross-fades with it (B6's '거울이' and its pause). Any cue with neither speed nor until uses base.

Easing from theme.ts: ease.out for appear, ease.exit for exit, ease.smooth for everything else, unless params say ease: linear. The two first-word cues that aren't entrances (B1's mirror glint, B3's dimming) are linear so they show within the 3-frame reaction window; smooth barely moves in 3 frames.
Stroke widths never scale with a figure's r: outlines 4 px, arrows 5 px with an 18 px head (theme stroke.arrow, mark.head) unless a taper scales them, the mirror frame 6 px (stroke.sheet).

Text: there is no text in the visual zone. Captions measured in Pretendard Bold 60 (static OTF advance widths, within 2 px of 002's browser measurement): widest '왜 위아래는 안 뒤집을까요?' 644 px, then '좌우가 바뀐 것처럼 보이죠.' 629 px; all fit one 800 px line.
Measured in the first render: B5's ghost ends 22 px left of my raised hand, the rings 29 px apart; bounds, centering and loop pass (check.md).

B5 dims me (0.3) from '내가' to B6's '거울이': the dashed copy turns over a faint me, so its outline and face read as its own (QA r1#1), and while the two stand side by side the eye goes up to their raised hands (cut critique).

components.name: Mirror
components.spec: A standing mirror seen from the front: a rectangle frame (6 px, in stroke, corner radius 20) around glass (filled in fill at 0.08), with two short parallel diagonal sheen streaks (5 px, text at 0.5, round caps, about 90 and 55 px long, 22 px apart, running from lower left to upper right) near its upper-right corner, inside x 790–900, y 290–420 for B1's mirror. Props: center, w, h (the frame's stroke centerline), stroke (default text), fill (default muted). Actions: appear (fade); exit; setStyle {opacity} (hides and restores it without ending it); pulse (a glint: the frame's stroke 2× and back and the sheen up to full opacity and back); tiltTo {deg} (tips back about its horizontal center line: the drawn height is h·cos(deg), centered on center's y; while tilting, the top edge is up to 6% shorter than the bottom (the most at 45°, none at 0° and 90°) so it reads as tipping back, not squashing; the glass fill and the sheen fade with cos(deg); at 90° it is a single horizontal line, w long, in the frame's stroke and color: B6's lake surface). It exposes its live glass (the frame's inner edge) for Person's inside.

components.name: Person
components.spec: A simple standing person drawn in code with one arm raised, seen from behind (view back: no face, hair covering the upper two thirds of the head) or from the front (view front: two eye dots and a short mouth line in text; the same hair over the top third), so the two views read as one person. Proportions in head radii r from the head's center `at`: shoulders at +1.9r, ±2.0r; waist at +5r, ±1.5r; two legs down to the feet at +11r; arms 0.45r thick with round ends; the raised arm goes up from the shoulder on the `raise` side (screenRight or screenLeft) to a hand centered at (±1.9r, −1.9r); the other arm hangs to (∓2.3r, +5.5r). The raised hand is an open hand, fingers up, 1.25r wide and 1.6r tall, its thumb out toward the body's midline (so both B1 hands have the thumb on the screen left); it shows one face: back (filled backColor at 0.6, 4 px stroke in backColor) or palm (filled palmColor at 0.6, stroke palmColor, three short palm lines in text at 0.6), the same outline either way. Nothing is drawn below y 1250 (the visual zone's bottom): a large figure low in the frame is cut there into a bust, with no line along the cut. Styles: solid (the body opaque, so nothing behind it shows through: filled muted at 0.5 over the background, outlined in text 4 px) or ghost (a dashed text outline 4 px, dash 18 gap 12, filled muted at 0.15; its raised hand filled as above at 0.8). Props: at, r, view, raise, face, backColor, palmColor, style. It exposes its live raised-hand center and size (for Ring and Hand). Actions: appear (fade); exit; setStyle {opacity} (hides and restores it without ending it); pulse {part: head | hand} (that part's stroke 2× and back, its fill brightened); turn (a half turn about the vertical line through at: the figure's horizontal scale runs cos from 1 through 0 to −1 across the span; at the midpoint the view switches back ↔ front and the raised hand's face back ↔ palm; it ends mirrored, the raised hand on the other screen side with its thumb still toward the body's midline, and raise reads the new side from then on); moveTo {at, r} (moves and scales about the head's center over the span; the cut stays at y 1250, so a bust that rises and shrinks shows its legs). Production additions: the turn swings the arms and hand with cos (the hand edge-on at the midpoint), narrows the torso only to its depth (theme figure.profile), keeps the head round while the hairline slides and the face fades in past the midpoint; the body is one silhouette outlined only outside; beneath: [ids] draws it just below those elements; inside: a Mirror id draws it only on that mirror's live glass.

components.name: DirArrow
components.spec: A straight direction arrow from `from` to `to` (screen points; the tip is at to) in color: a 5 px shaft with an 18 px head, both scaled along the arrow from taper[0] at the tail to taper[1] at the head (default [1, 1]), so an arrow going into the picture narrows and one coming out widens. Could be built by generalizing Arrow (which aims between bodies and tethers). Props: from, to, color, taper. Actions: appear (grows from its tail); exit; setStyle {opacity} (dims, hides and restores it without ending it); pulse (stroke and head 1.6× and back).

components.name: Ring
components.spec: A circle outline that marks something: 5 px in color, radius r, centered on `at` or on a Person's live raised-hand center (`of`: its id). Props: of or at, r, color. Actions: appear (drawn on clockwise from 12 o'clock); exit; pulse (stroke 2× and back).

components.name: Scenery
components.spec: Landscape drawn in code, standing on a waterline. Items: mountain {points} (a polygon whose first and last points are its base on the waterline; outlined in text 4 px along the silhouette only, never along the base; filled muted at 0.35; a snowcap filled text at 0.8 over the top 20% of its height) and tree {x, base, height, width} (a conifer: a muted trunk 10 px wide from base up 0.2 × height, then three stacked triangles, the lowest `width` wide, up to base − height; filled muted at 0.35, outlined text 4 px). With flipAbout: y, everything is mirrored about that horizontal line (upside down below it); opacity scales the whole drawing. Props: items, flipAbout, opacity. Actions: appear (fade; with params.unfold, it grows out of the flip line: vertical scale 0 → 1 about flipAbout, so a reflection hangs down out of the water); exit; pulse (outline 2× and back, fill brightened).
